summary: Over the 14-day period, CGM data showed an overall time-in-range of 86.0%, with a coefficient of variation of 32.6%. A recurring pattern of hypoglycemia was identified in the overnight hours (local 01:00 hour time-below-range 18.5%) and occasionally in the early evening (local 19:00 hour time-below-range 15.3%). The automated insulin delivery system (AAPS) actively reduced basal delivery to zero during these periods, indicating that the scheduled basal rates may be contributing to the low episodes. Daytime glucose rises (e.g., peak average 162 mg/dL at 16:00) were managed without significant hypoglycemia. No carbohydrate entries were recorded during the period, preventing evaluation of meal bolus strategy, carbohydrate ratios, or e-carb use. The primary recommendation is to lower the overnight basal rate from 00:00 to 05:00 to reduce hypoglycemia risk.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall TIR 86.0%, time above 8.9%, time below 5.1%, CV 32.6%. Notable hypoglycemia risk: the lowest recorded glucose was 41 mg/dL (Aug 14), and several days had >5% below range (Aug 11: 9.4%, Aug 18: 12.8%). Overnight hours (01:00) and early evening (19:00) show elevated below-range percentages. Any recommendations must prioritize avoiding deeper hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary, daily_glucose, hourly_glucose_local (01:00 below 18.5%, 19:00 below 15.3%), glucose_extremes.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal (0.6 U/h 00:00-05:00, 0.7 U/h 05:00-06:00) is frequently overridden by AAPS zero temp basals, yet hypoglycemia persists (01:00 below 18.5%). This may be partly due to residual IOB from daytime corrections, but lowering the scheduled basal is a safe initial step. Mid-day glucose rises (avg 162 mg/dL at 16:00) may reflect unannounced carbohydrate intake rather than basal insufficiency. Evening lows (19:00 below 15.3%) could be influenced by the 0.5 U/h basal (16:00-18:00) and 0.6 U/h (18:00-19:00). Targets (90-100 mg/dL) appear appropriate.

analysis_steps.findings: The dominant actionable pattern is overnight hypoglycemia. While residual IOB from daytime corrections may contribute, the scheduled basal rate (0.6 U/h 00:00-05:00) appears too high because the algorithm frequently sets zero temp basals yet lows still occur. Lowering this basal segment is a safe first change. Meal strategies cannot be addressed until carbohydrate logging begins. All AAPS automation settings are appropriate and are kept.

recommendations.title: Reduce early overnight basal rate
recommendations.description: The scheduled basal rate from 00:00 to 05:00 (0.6 U/h) contributes to overnight lows despite AAPS frequently suspending insulin. Lowering it to 0.5 U/h may reduce hypoglycemia risk while allowing the algorithm to increase delivery if needed.

recommendations.title: Begin logging all carbohydrate intake
recommendations.description: Without carbohydrate records, meal timing, prebolus, and CR cannot be evaluated or optimized. Enter carbs for all meals and snacks in the system to enable future adjustments.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Reduce the basal rate from 00:00 to 05:00 from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h. Keep all other basal segments unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Persistent overnight hypoglycemia (time-below-range 18.5% at 01:00 local) despite AAPS frequently issuing zero temp basals suggests the scheduled rate is too high. A reduction of 0.1 U/h is a conservative first step that prioritises safety. IOB from daytime corrections may still cause some lows, so close monitoring is needed.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After 3 nights on the new basal rate, review overnight CGM traces. If time-below-range remains >5%, consider further reducing the following basal segment (05:00-06:00) or evaluate timing of daytime correction doses.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Begin logging carbohydrate entries for all meals and snacks immediately. Until carb data are available, no prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, SMB/UAM meal interaction, or e-carb strategy can be recommended. The AAPS UAM will continue to handle unannounced meals.

meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Logging carbohydrate intake (grams and timing) for at least 3 days will enable review of postprandial responses and assessment of prebolus timing and CR.

implementation_steps: 1. Discuss the proposed basal rate change with your healthcare team.
2. In your AAPS profile, reduce the basal rate from 00:00 to 05:00 from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h.
3. Keep all other basal segments, targets, CR, ISF, DIA, and automation settings unchanged.
4. Monitor overnight CGM traces closely for the next 3 nights, paying special attention to time-below-range at 01:00-02:00.
5. If hypoglycemia persists (>5% below range overnight), consider a further reduction to the 05:00-06:00 basal segment or evaluate if daytime correction bolus timing is contributing to IOB overnight.
6. Begin entering carbohydrate amounts for every meal and snack in the Nightscout/AAPS system to enable future meal strategy analysis.
education: During fasting periods, AAPS can set a temporary basal rate of 0 U/h to prevent lows; if the scheduled basal is too high, the system will repeatedly suspend insulin, but some lows may still occur if IOB from earlier boluses remains.
Dynamic ISF is a feature that automatically adjusts your insulin sensitivity factor based on current glucose trends; it helps compensate for mismatches in your static ISF

Without logging carbohydrates, the system cannot calculate meal insulin needs accurately; UAM (unannounced meal detection) can provide some coverage, but dedicated meal boluses usually give better control.
safety_notes: This report provides decision-support suggestions only; always verify any changes independently and consult your healthcare provider before making adjustments.
Change only one insulin delivery setting at a time. After adjusting the basal rate, wait several days and review CGM data before making further modifications.
Monitor glucose closely, especially during sleep, when implementing a basal rate change. Have fast-acting carbohydrates immediately available.
Be aware that residual insulin-on-board from daytime corrections can still contribute to overnight lows, even after a basal reduction.
